title: The importance of bees
paragraphs: How do you feel about bees? Do you get irritated when they buzz around you and do you fear their mission is just to sting you? Love them or loathe them, these little insects are extremely important creatures, and without them we might starve. Bees deserve some respect – they give us honey, and they play their part either pollinating the many vegetables and fruits we eat directly or pollinating the food for the animals that we then consume. In fact, they are the world’s most important pollinators. That’s not all – a study by the University of Reading in the UK, found bees and other pollinating insects have a global economic value of around £120bn ($150bn) and contribute around £690m ($850m) to the UK economy every year.

So, bees are worth protecting, and although a small number of bee species are vital for crops such as oilseed rape, apples and strawberries, experts say we should be taking care of all our bees. Researchers say conservation efforts should be aimed at a wide number of species – even those that currently contribute little to crop pollination – in order to maintain biodiversity and ensure future food security.

Unfortunately, in recent times, bee populations have been declining due to pesticides, parasites, disease and habitat loss. It’s something we should be worried about because, as Gill Perkins, chief executive of the Bumblebee Conservation Trust, told BBC Future website: “They provide a whole ecosystem service.” The recent lockdowns caused by the coronavirus pandemic seem to have given bee populations a little boost because they faced less human disturbance, traffic and polluting fumes.

Conservationists hope, going forward, people will appreciate bees more and encourage them to thrive as they reconnect with nature. Gill Perkins says, “They are beginning to realise how their mental health and wellbeing is supported by nature – particularly by bumblebees, which are so iconic and beautiful and buzzy.”
So, it really seems time to give bees a second chance.

vocabulary.example: A bee flew into the open window.
vocabulary.translation: 一只蜜蜂飞进了开着的窗户。

vocabulary.example: A wasp was buzzing around the picnic table.
vocabulary.translation: 一只黄蜂在野餐桌周围嗡嗡作响。

vocabulary.example: I got stung by a bee while picking flowers.
vocabulary.translation: 我摘花的时候被蜜蜂蛰了一下。

vocabulary.example: Ants, bees and butterflies are all insects.
vocabulary.translation: 蚂蚁、蜜蜂和蝴蝶都是昆虫。

vocabulary.example: She spread honey on her toast for breakfast.
vocabulary.translation: 她早餐时把蜂蜜涂在了吐司上。

vocabulary.example: Pollination is essential for the reproduction of many plants.
vocabulary.translation: 传粉对许多植物的繁殖至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: pollinator /ˈpɒləneɪtə(r)/ n. 传粉者；授粉媒介
vocabulary.example: Bees are the most important pollinator for most fruit crops.
vocabulary.translation: 蜜蜂是大多数水果作物最重要的传粉者。

vocabulary.entry: economic /ˌiːkəˈnɒmɪk/ adj. 经济的；经济上的
vocabulary.example: The project has brought many economic benefits to the region.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目为该地区带来了诸多经济效益。

vocabulary.example: This rare species of plant is found only in the rainforest.
vocabulary.translation: 这种珍稀植物物种只在雨林中存在。

vocabulary.example: Wheat is a major crop grown in this part of the country.
vocabulary.translation: 小麦是该国这个地区种植的主要农作物。

vocabulary.example: The government has introduced new laws for wildlife conservation.
vocabulary.translation: 政府出台了新的野生动物保护法。

vocabulary.example: Protecting rainforests is crucial for maintaining global biodiversity.
vocabulary.translation: 保护雨林对维护全球生物多样性至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: food security /ˈfuːd sɪˈkjʊərəti/ n. 粮食安全
vocabulary.example: The organization works to improve food security in developing countries.
vocabulary.translation: 该组织致力于改善发展中国家的粮食安全状况。

vocabulary.example: The use of pesticide has been restricted to protect the environment.
vocabulary.translation: 为了保护环境，杀虫剂的使用已受到限制。

vocabulary.example: The parasite lives on the blood of its host.
vocabulary.translation: 这种寄生虫靠吸食宿主的血液为生。

vocabulary.example: The disease has spread rapidly among the local bee population.
vocabulary.translation: 这种疾病在当地的蜜蜂种群中迅速传播开来。

vocabulary.example: The destruction of forest is threatening the animal’s natural habitat.
vocabulary.translation: 森林的破坏正威胁着这种动物的自然栖息地。

vocabulary.example: The forest ecosystem is home to thousands of species.
vocabulary.translation: 森林生态系统是数千个物种的家园。

vocabulary.example: We need to avoid any disturbance to the nesting birds.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要避免对筑巢鸟类造成任何干扰。

vocabulary.entry: fume /fjuːm/ n. 有害气体；尾气
vocabulary.example: Car fumes are one of the main causes of air pollution.
vocabulary.translation: 汽车尾气是空气污染的主要成因之一。

vocabulary.entry: conservationist /ˌkɒnsəˈveɪʃnɪst/ n. 环保人士；生态保护者
vocabulary.example: The conservationist is trying to save the endangered species.
vocabulary.translation: 这位环保人士正努力拯救这种濒危物种。

vocabulary.entry: wellbeing /ˈwel biːɪŋ/ n. 健康；福祉
vocabulary.example: Spending time in nature is good for both physical and mental wellbeing.
vocabulary.translation: 亲近自然有益于身心健康。

vocabulary.entry: iconic /aɪˈkɒnɪk/ adj. 标志性的；具有代表性的
vocabulary.example: The Eiffel Tower is an iconic symbol of Paris.
vocabulary.translation: 埃菲尔铁塔是巴黎的标志性象征。

vocabulary.example: She loathes the smell of cigarette smoke.
vocabulary.translation: 她厌恶香烟的气味。

vocabulary.example: Everyone should contribute to the protection of the environment.
vocabulary.translation: 每个人都应该为环境保护贡献自己的力量。

sentences.english: How do you feel about bees?
Do you get irritated when they buzz around you and do you fear their mission is just to sting you?
sentences.chinese: 当它们在你身边嗡嗡作响时，你会感到烦躁吗？你会担心它们的目的就是蛰你吗？

sentences.english: Love them or loathe them, these little insects are extremely important creatures, and without them we might starve.
sentences.chinese: 无论你是喜欢还是讨厌它们，这些小小的昆虫都是极其重要的生物，没有它们，人类可能会面临饥荒。

sentences.english: Bees deserve some respect – they give us honey, and they play their part either pollinating the many vegetables and fruits we eat directly or pollinating the food for the animals that we then consume.
sentences.chinese: 蜜蜂值得我们尊重——它们为我们酿造蜂蜜，还承担着重要的传粉工作：要么直接为我们食用的各类蔬果传粉，要么为我们饲养的动物所吃的饲料作物传粉。

sentences.english: In fact, they are the world’s most important pollinators.
sentences.chinese: 事实上，蜜蜂是全球最重要的传粉者。

sentences.english: That’s not all – a study by the University of Reading in the UK, found bees and other pollinating insects have a global economic value of around £120bn ($150bn) and contribute around £690m ($850m) to the UK economy every year.
sentences.chinese: 不仅如此，英国雷丁大学的一项研究发现，蜜蜂及其他传粉昆虫的全球经济价值约为1200亿英镑（合1500亿美元），每年为英国经济贡献约6.9亿英镑（合8.5亿美元）。

sentences.english: So, bees are worth protecting, and although a small number of bee species are vital for crops such as oilseed rape, apples and strawberries, experts say we should be taking care of all our bees.
sentences.chinese: 因此，蜜蜂值得被保护。尽管只有少数几种蜜蜂对油菜、苹果、草莓这类作物的生长至关重要，但专家表示，我们应当保护所有种类的蜜蜂。

sentences.english: Researchers say conservation efforts should be aimed at a wide number of species – even those that currently contribute little to crop pollination – in order to maintain biodiversity and ensure future food security.
sentences.chinese: 研究人员指出，为了维护生物多样性、保障未来的粮食安全，保护工作应覆盖更多的蜜蜂物种，哪怕是那些目前对农作物传粉贡献甚微的种类。

sentences.english: Unfortunately, in recent times, bee populations have been declining due to pesticides, parasites, disease and habitat loss.
sentences.chinese: 遗憾的是，近年来由于杀虫剂的使用、寄生虫侵扰、疾病传播以及栖息地丧失等因素，蜜蜂的数量一直在减少。

sentences.english: It’s something we should be worried about because, as Gill Perkins, chief executive of the Bumblebee Conservation Trust, told BBC Future website: “They provide a whole ecosystem service.”
sentences.chinese: 这一现象值得我们警惕，正如大黄蜂保护信托基金的首席执行官吉尔·珀金斯在接受BBC未来频道采访时所说：“蜜蜂提供着完整的生态系统服务。”

sentences.english: The recent lockdowns caused by the coronavirus pandemic seem to have given bee populations a little boost because they faced less human disturbance, traffic and polluting fumes.
sentences.chinese: 新冠疫情期间实施的封锁措施，似乎让蜜蜂数量有了小幅回升，因为它们受到的人类干扰、交通影响以及尾气污染都有所减少。

sentences.english: Conservationists hope, going forward, people will appreciate bees more and encourage them to thrive as they reconnect with nature.
sentences.chinese: 环保人士希望，在未来，随着人们重新亲近自然，大家能更加珍惜蜜蜂，助力它们繁衍兴旺。

sentences.english: Gill Perkins says, “They are beginning to realise how their mental health and wellbeing is supported by nature – particularly by bumblebees, which are so iconic and beautiful and buzzy.”
sentences.chinese: 吉尔·珀金斯表示：“人们开始意识到，我们的心理健康和整体福祉都依赖于大自然——尤其是那些标志性的、美丽的、嗡嗡作响的大黄蜂。”

sentences.english: So, it really seems time to give bees a second chance.
sentences.chinese: 所以，现在确实是时候给蜜蜂更多的关注与呵护了。
